text.p: Philippine holding firm A. Soriano Corp (Anscor) said on Wednesday it was restructuring its investments to concentrate on its more profitable interests.

Anscor chairman Andres Soriano III told shareholders at the annual meeting prospects for the company were brighter this year with its entry into new businesses with "potential for high value appreciation," such as home cable, cement manufacturing and health care services.
Anscor posted record net income of 463.364 million pesos in 1996 against 307.358 million the previous year.
"Your company is presently in the process of restructing and realigning its other investments in its portfolio," Soriano said.
The strategy involve the sale, merger or spin-off of Anscor's smaller investments, he added.
Analysts praised the announcements saying the company was bound to benefit.

"The efforts would enable Anscor to concentrate in its core businesses that include cargo handling, banking and financial services, and cable manufacturing," Dharmala Securities Philippines Inc analyst Ben Hermoso said.

As part of its restructuring, Anscor has written off from its books its investment in Atlas Consolidated Mining and Development Corp, whose major copper mine in the central Cebu City was closed three years ago due to soft copper prices and steep production costs.
Anscor president Jose Ibazeta said Atlas was negotiating with an Australian group for the revival of its Carmen copper mine in Cebu.
Shareholders of Anscor approved the board's proposal to float convertible notes to give the company flexibility to invests in new projects in the future.
The company plans to use part of the proceeds of its 2.2 billion pesos rights issue and the proposed convertible note issuance either by June or September this year to fund new investments.
"Depending on market conditions, we can raise at least $60 to $100 million from the convertible notes," said Ernest Cuyegkeng, Anscor's chief finance officer.
Soriano said Anscor will be "looking at all (investment) opportunities" such as power generation. The company plans to submit a bid for the privatisation of the National Power Corp.

"We are confident that the refocus of several of our activities, further growth of our core business will result in continued growth and increased shareholder values," Soriano said. -- Manila newsroom (632) 841-89-36, fax 817-62-67
